newsitem.title: UK: UK domestic gas competition to extend to Scotland.
newsitem.headline: UK domestic gas competition to extend to Scotland.

text.p: Britain's drive to extend domestic gas competition took a step forward this morning when the Department of Trade and Industry on Monday announced it would be extended to Scotland later this year.

Britain plans to deregulate domestic gas supply nationwide during 1998, and has already introduced pilot schemes in the south western counties of Devon, Cornwall and Somerset last year, and in Avon, Dorset, East and West Sussex this year.
It had originally been planned to delay extending competition further until next year. But a spokesman for industry regulator Ofgas said on Monday that the regulator welcomed speeding up the process.
"We've long been in favour of introducing the benefits of competition, and rather sooner than later," he said. "We welcome the way forward."

Board of Trade President Ian Lang plans to lay an order in parliament on Monday, and, depending on approval by Ofgas, competition could start in October. Ofgas confirmed there was unlikely to be any delay from the regulator's side as "we very much welcome the order."
A number of gas supply companies already have Ofgas-issued licences to supply gas to domestic consumers anywhere in the country, and will be able to do so as soon as Scotland's deregulation starts.

These are British Gas Trading, part of Centrica Plc ; Eastern Natural Gas; London Total Energy; Northern Electric Plc; NORWEB; Southern Electric Gas ; Scottish Power Plc, for everywhere except the first pilot area; and Texaco Inc and Calor Group Plc, trading as Calortex.
Lang was quoted as saying on a radio interview on Monday morning that competition in gas supply in Scotland would mean a reduction in the average gas bill of 65 stg to 70 stg a year.
Shadow Energy Minister John Battle on Monday added Labour's support for gas competition but condemned the government's handling of its introduction.

"If today's proposal were a serious attempt to improve the process of introducing competition, why have they announced it with so little warning either to the industry or, this close to a general election, the Opposition parties?" he asked.
"The Conservatives have not properly learnt from or consulted upon the trials of gas competition which have been conducted in the South West," he added.
